topic: From Average Speed to Instantaneous Rate: Understanding the Derivative

outline.topic: From Average Speed to Instantaneous Rate: Understanding the Derivative

sections.title: The Hook: The Speeding Cheetah
sections.content: Introduce a cheetah sprinting. We know the total distance and total time, but how do we know if it was speeding at a specific micro-moment? Connect average speed (total distance/total time) to the need for a more precise measurement.
sections.example: A cheetah runs 100 meters in 5 seconds. Average speed is 20 m/s, but what was its speed exactly at the 2-second mark?

sections.title: Visualizing the Slope of a Secant Line
sections.content: Use a position-time graph (parabolic curve). Draw a secant line passing through two points (t1, t2). Explain that the slope of this line represents the 'Average Rate of Change'.
sections.example: A graph showing a blue curve (distance) with a straight red secant line connecting two dots, labeled 'Rise/Run'.

sections.title: The Limiting Process: Getting Closer
sections.content: Animate the second point moving closer to the first point. As the interval Δt shrinks toward zero, the secant line transforms. This is the conceptual birth of the tangent line.
sections.example: Animation: The red secant line rotates and flattens as the second point 'slides' along the curve toward the first point.

sections.title: Defining the Derivative
sections.content: Formalize the concept: The derivative is the limit of the average rate of change as Δt approaches 0. Introduce the notation f'(x) as the 'instantaneous slope'.
sections.example: Mathematical formula: f'(x) = lim(h→0) [f(x+h) - f(x)] / h, overlaid on the static tangent line.

sections.title: Application & Wrap-up
sections.content: Summarize how the derivative is a 'magnifying glass' for change. Revisit the cheetah: the slope of the tangent line at exactly t=2 gives the instantaneous speed.
sections.example: Display the final tangent line at t=2 on the cheetah's graph, labeled 'Instantaneous Velocity: 24 m/s'.

storyboard.title: The Hook: The Speeding Cheetah
lecture_lines: A cheetah runs 100 meters in 5 seconds.
Average speed is 20 meters per second.
Was it speeding at the 2-second mark?
animations: Show a cheetah sprinting across the screen. (Color: #FF4500)
Highlight the cheetah's change in position over time. (Color: #00BFFF)
Animate a graph plotting position versus time. (Color: #FFFFFF)

storyboard.title: Visualizing the Slope of a Secant Line
lecture_lines: Plot position versus time as a curve.
Connect two points with a secant line.
The slope shows average rate of change.
animations: Draw a smooth curve representing a function. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Place two points on the curve. (Color: #FFD700)
Draw a straight secant line connecting those points. (Color: #32CD32)

storyboard.title: The Limiting Process: Getting Closer
lecture_lines: Slide the second point toward the first.
It flattens into a tangent line.
animations: Move the second point closer to the first point. (Color: #FFD700)
Show the secant line updating as points converge. (Color: #32CD32)
Fade the secant line into a tangent line. (Color: #FF4500)

storyboard.title: Defining the Derivative
lecture_lines: Let the time interval shrink to zero.
This gives us the instantaneous slope.
animations: Display the derivative formula clearly on screen. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Label the components of the limit expression. (Color: #00BFFF)

storyboard.title: Application & Wrap-up
lecture_lines: The derivative acts like a magnifying glass.
It measures change at a single moment.
The cheetah's speed at two seconds is 24.
animations: Show the tangent line on a real-world graph. (Color: #32CD32)
Label the tangent line as 'Instantaneous Velocity'. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Fade screen to black with title. (Color: #FFFFFF)
